subject: Renewal orchestration: staggered multi-year ramp + auto-renew opt-in
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-06-01T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal orchestration proposal for Nimble — staggered multi-year + auto-opt path

Team,

Following our QBR with Nimble last week they asked for a renewal that: 1) smooths their fiscal alignment across two product teams, 2) gives them predictable unit economics as they scale, and 3) preserves an opt-in auto-renew option after year one. I put together a thin orchestration proposal attached (nimble_renewal_staggered_proposal_v3.pdf) with two pillars:

- Staggered multi-year ramp: Year 1 = conservative committed capacity with milestone-based step-ups at months 6 and 12. Year 2-3 = annualized committed buckets with optional burst lanes.
- Auto-renew opt-in: auto-renew clause triggers only if utilization > 70% over the trailing 90 days and with a 60‑day notice window for them to opt-out.

Operational asks: legal will need a short amendment for the auto-opt clause (simple opt-out language and notice cadence). Ops needs to confirm we can route their account into a dedicated burst pool for predicted spikes. Finance: proposed blended rate across three years with a 5% year-over-year protection.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment on legal language and billing cadence by EOD Friday.
2) Share the deck and proposal with Alex (Nimble) once legal signs off; target signature timeline: 2 weeks.

Notes: I added a tentative milestone table in the spreadsheet (nimble_MA_plan.xlsx) for CS onboarding and ramp metrics.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Re: Renewal orchestration proposal for Nimble — staggered multi-year + auto-opt path

Karthik — thanks for pulling this together, looks clean. A few quick notes from ops and product: 

- Staggered windows are fine but request we lock the step-up triggers to a clear metric (we suggest 50M tokens/month sustained for 4 consecutive weeks OR monthly 95th percentile latency impact < 150ms).
- For the burst lanes, ops wants explicit max burst capacity and preferred fallback (if burst pool exhausted, fallback to higher-latency queued path vs. throttling).
- Regarding auto-renew: product prefers a shorter measurement window (45 days) to avoid long tails; legal usually pushes back on auto-enrollment language — we should keep the ask as an "auto-offer" with opt-in via a docsign acceptance unless Nimble explicitly checks opt-in box in the first renewal.

I'm copying Ben for pricing impact and Marissa for contract cadence. If you want, I can draft the fallback/ops clause today and Marissa can lead legal language.

Camila
Camila Reyes
VP, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Thanks, all. I like the milestone-driven approach; couple of procurement/legal bullets from my side:

- Legal redline ask: keep the auto-renew as an "offer" rather than automatic enrollment. We can provide a one-click opt-in in DocuSign that appears at signature for the first renewal. Language: "Customer may elect to enroll in an auto-renew program subject to utilization thresholds and a 60-day notice period prior to renewal. Enrollment occurs only upon signing the Auto-Renew Addendum."
- Billing cadence: Finance requests we align invoice calendar to Nimble's fiscal quarters starting July 1. That will require proration for the first period — include a one-time adjustment credit on the first invoice.
- Risk: if they underutilize year 1 heavily there should be a true-up at month 12 with a 90-day close window. Suggest we keep true-up mechanics identical to other multi-year deals for consistency.

If Ben can confirm the blended rates and credit math, I can prepare a short amendment template and loop legal. If everyone agrees, I'll run to legal and Ops and aim to have the redlines back by Tuesday EOD.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
